key_insight: External strain can strongly tune electron and hole g-factors in bulk CsPbX3, even driving them through zero, while nanocrystals are much less strain-sensitive because of quantum confinement.
engineering_relevance: This suggests strain engineering could be a practical knob for controlling spin-dependent properties in lead-halide perovskite devices, with bulk materials offering the largest tunability.
method: Built an 18-band k·p model for cubic CsPbX3.
Fit model parameters to target band structures from DFT calculations.
Used linear response and real-space calculations to evaluate strain-dependent g-factors in bulk and nanocrystals.
evidence_signal: The study is theoretical and compares model predictions against DFT-derived band structures, then evaluates g-factor trends under external strain.
watch_item: Results are for the reference cubic phase and theory-based nanocrystal models, so real devices may differ due to disorder, phase changes, and fabrication-dependent strain.
paper_title: Strain tunability of electron and hole g-factors in CsPb$X_3$: bulk and nanocrystals
